jobs.title: Executive Director, Clinical Operations
jobs.description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

Job Description

Reporting to the Executive Vice President and Chief Clinical Officer (CCO), the Executive Director, Clinical Operations serves as a strategic operational partner to the CCO and the Office of the Chief Clinical Officer (OCCO) at Beth Israel Lahey Health (BILH). This role is responsible for translating the CCO’s strategic priorities into coordinated, system-level action across a large, complex portfolio spanning clinical quality, patient safety, behavioral health, primary care, value-based care, managed care, and digital health and innovation.

The Executive Director, Clinical Operations will serve as the operational nerve center for the OCCO, ensuring that the CCO’s agenda is advanced with rigor, timeliness, and alignment across a team of approximately 15 direct reports and their respective organizations. The position will directly manage a portfolio of high-priority enterprise initiatives, coordinate the CCO’s leadership forums including joint CMO/CNO governance meetings, oversee budget management and financial reporting for the OCCO, and lead the performance management cycle including quality dashboards, KPI tracking, and leadership evaluations.

This role requires an exceptional leader who combines executive-level business acumen with deep healthcare operational knowledge, the ability to build and maintain trusted relationships across all levels of the organization, and the discipline to drive accountability and execution in a large integrated health system.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & CCO Office Operations

Serve as the primary operational advisor and thought partner to the CCO, providing strategic counsel on organizational priorities, resource deployment, and leadership effectiveness
Manage the day-to-day operational rhythm of the OCCO, including agenda management, decision tracking, and follow-through on commitments across the CCO’s portfolio
Maintain comprehensive situational awareness of enterprise-wide clinical, operational, and strategic activities relevant to the CCO’s agenda; proactively surface issues, risks, and opportunities
Prepare and staff the CCO for executive meetings, board presentations, and external engagements including synthesis of materials, briefings, and pre-reads
Represent the CCO in select cross-functional meetings and workgroups; serve as a trusted proxy with authority to advance decisions in the CCO’s absence

Direct Report & Team Leadership Support

Partner with the CCO to manage an executive team of approximately 15 direct reports spanning clinical quality, patient safety, primary care, behavioral health, managed care, digital health, and innovation
Coordinate an integrated leadership calendar for the OCCO including team meetings, one-on-ones, leadership forums, and performance check-ins
Lead the annual performance evaluation cycle for the CCO’s direct reports including goal-setting alignment, mid-year reviews, year-end assessments, and competency documentation
Facilitate onboarding and integration of new direct reports and senior hires into the CCO’s organizational structure
Identify and address gaps in team communication, coordination, and accountability across the OCCO leadership team

Budget Management & Financial Oversight

Oversee budget planning, monitoring, and reporting for the Office of the Chief Clinical Officer and its affiliated functions
Coordinate the annual budget development process for OCCO cost centers in partnership with Finance; establish timelines, templates, and submission requirements
Track budget-to-actual performance on a monthly basis; produce executive summaries and variance analyses for the CCO and CFO
Manage capital and operational budget requests across the OCCO portfolio, ensuring alignment with enterprise financial planning cycles
Support development of business cases, ROI analyses, and investment proposals for new initiatives within the clinical enterprise

Project & Initiative Portfolio Management

Maintain a master inventory of enterprise projects and initiatives within the CCO’s portfolio; establish governance structures, timelines, milestones, and accountability frameworks
Directly manage a set of high-priority, cross-functional initiatives on behalf of the CCO, including program design, stakeholder coordination, and implementation oversight
Track and report on the status of strategic initiatives, escalating risks and barriers to the CCO and relevant forums in a timely manner
Coordinate with System Services, clinical operations, finance, IT, and other functions to align project resources and resolve cross-cutting execution challenges
Apply structured project management methodologies and shared digital platforms to ensure disciplined planning, accountability, and organizational learning

Clinical Quality & Performance Management

Coordinate the CCO’s quality and patient safety governance activities, including support for the annual goal-setting cycle, enterprise quality plan, and KPI alignment across clinical domains
Oversee development and production of quality performance dashboards in partnership with Quality, Analytics, and IT, including CMS Star Ratings tracking, HCAHPS/patient experience metrics, and safety indicators
Support preparation for Joint Commission surveys, regulatory reviews, and accreditation activities as they relate to the CCO’s portfolio
Facilitate preparation and follow-through for quality committee meetings, Quality and Patient Safety Board reporting, and the Q-PECA cycle
Coordinate the integration of value-based care performance metrics into the CCO’s broader quality and safety management framework

CMO/CNO Governance & Leadership Forums

Plan and manage the operational structure of joint CMO/CNO governance forums, including agenda development, pre-read preparation, action item tracking, and follow-through
Coordinate cross-functional leadership meetings involving the CCO, Chief Medical Officers, Chief Nursing Officers, and clinical operations leaders across BILH’s hospital and ambulatory enterprise
Support design and facilitation of leadership retreats, strategic planning sessions, and executive team offsites within the OCCO portfolio
Ensure effective multidirectional communication between the OCCO and clinical leadership across BILH’s 14 hospitals and their affiliated ambulatory networks
Work with divisional CMOs and CNOs to coordinate system-level clinical initiatives, identify common themes, and surface constructive feedback to the CCO

Data Governance & Innovation

Partner with IT, Analytics, and Finance to develop and maintain data governance standards that support clinical performance monitoring across the OCCO portfolio
Drive adoption of shared digital platforms and reporting tools that standardize how the OCCO accesses, interprets, and communicates performance data
Support the CCO’s digital health and healthcare innovation agenda, including coordination of the BILH Launchpad and related strategic partnerships
Identify and advance opportunities for AI-enabled tools and analytics to enhance clinical operations and performance management within the CCO’s portfolio

Minimum Qualifications

Education

BA/BS required. Master’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, or a related field strongly preferred.

Experience

10+ years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare management, clinical operations, strategy, or management consulting
Demonstrated experience operating in a complex, matrixed health system environment at the system or enterprise level
Prior experience in a Chief of Staff, VP of Operations, or senior strategy/operations role in a major health system or academic medical center strongly preferred
Experience managing budgets, performance cycles, and senior leadership teams
Familiarity with clinical quality, value-based care, patient experience, and population health management

Skills, Knowledge & Abilities

Exceptional organizational intelligence and political acuity; ability to navigate complexity, build consensus, and advance priorities across diverse constituencies
Superior written and oral communication skills, including executive-level briefing, presentation development, and board-ready materials
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent high-stakes initiatives with precision and disciplined follow-through
Strong analytical skills, including financial analysis, performance data interpretation, and translation of complex data into actionable insights
Deep knowledge of healthcare operations, clinical governance structures, and regulatory and accreditation frameworks
Proficiency with project management tools, performance dashboards, and digital collaboration platforms
High degree of professional integrity and discretion; ability to handle sensitive organizational and personnel matters with confidentiality
Collaborative leadership style with the ability to inspire a high-performing team and create a culture of accountability and excellence

Pay Range

$190,000.00 USD - $250,000.00 USD

Actual compensation is determined based on several factors, that may include seniority, education, training, relevant experience, relevant certifications, geography of work location, job responsibilities, or other applicable factors permissible by law.

jobs.description:
Working/Functional Title

Director of Development, CANR

Position Summary

Are you passionate about building relationships and securing major gifts for interdisciplinary research that tackles pressing global challenges? The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at Michigan State University is the largest STEM academic unit. It is a dynamic interdisciplinary powerhouse focused on solving global challenges that reach far beyond traditional agriculture. The college, along with MSU Extension and AgBio Research, serves as an epicenter of innovation that tackles pressing global issues such as climate science, sustainability, urban planning, food security, and public health.

The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at Michigan State University is seeking a talented and ambitious individual to join our collaborative development team as the Director of Development.

In this results-oriented position, you’ll play a critical role in shaping the future of STEM education and research. You’ll leverage your strategic thinking and interpersonal skills to cultivate relationships with alumni and friends, securing vital resources that fuel innovation and opportunity in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.

What will you do?

Become a champion for the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources and Michigan State University by raising support for cutting-edge research with a real-world impact across multiple fields: You’ll manage a portfolio of 75 - 100 prospects, fostering long-term relationships that elevate the College’s reputation and fuel its success.
Uncover hidden potential: Employ your keen eye for discovery to identify new alumni and donors, building a robust pipeline for future giving.
Leverage your strategic planning experience: Develop and execute personalized cultivation and stewardship strategies, averaging 12-15 strategic face-to-face visits and 2-4 solicitations per month.
Collaborate for collective success: Partner with faculty, college leadership, and internal stakeholders to deepen relationships and maximize your impact.
Be a part of and learn from a team dedicated to building a cohesive culture: Work alongside a high-performing development team, sharing best practices and celebrating collective achievements.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

Make a tangible difference: Your efforts will directly translate into increased resources that empower students, faculty, research, and programs in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources, AgBio Research, and MSU Extension.
Join a collaborative environment: We foster a supportive and team-oriented atmosphere where you’ll be empowered to grow and excel.
Be part of a prestigious institution: You’ll have the privilege of donning Spartan green and white, while representing the land grant mission to provide high-quality education, conduct research, and engage with the public to advance knowledge and improve lives.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Director of Development will manage a portfolio of 75-100 major and principal gift donor prospects, focusing efforts on prospects whose philanthropic capacity is $100,000 or more to maximize the fundraising potential within the College and on behalf of Michigan State University. Additionally, the Director will oversee and manage the Associate and Assistant Directors of Development, providing leadership, mentorship, and strategic direction to ensure their success in advancing the college's development goals.

The Director will average 12-15 strategic visits per month, resulting in greater engagement and movement toward a major gift solicitation at a rate of 2 to 4 solicitations per month, with all solicitation efforts cleared and coordinated with the college and University Advancement at Michigan State University. A significant amount of the Director’s time will be dedicated to traveling out of state and managing prospect activity within a few major metro areas.

The duties of the Director of Development are as follows, but are not limited to:

Fundraising -

Engage in the identification, cultivation, and solicitation of gifts, mainly from individuals, as well as some corporations and professional groups in support of the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources' strategic and campaign priorities.
Collaborate and coordinate with University Advancement, administrators, and faculty in the college to create and carry out fundraising strategies and solicitation of gifts of $100,000 and more.
Identify and maintain an active pool of 75 prospects under strategic management.
Achieve college fundraising goals through an active and consistent program of prospect and donor outreach that includes 180 significant contacts annually.
Utilize phone calls, email, mail, social media, and other strategies to identify, connect with, and engage alumni with the goal of soliciting financial support.
Identify, qualify, and work to build strong, engaged relationships with major gift prospects to determine and merge prospect passions, interests, and needs with the college’s funding priority areas.
Schedule joint prospect visits with members of college leadership, faculty, or other Development colleagues.
Serve as a liaison officer between the unit and donors and potential donors to ensure that such information and services as may be desired are provided to the full extent permitted by university policy, rules, and regulations.
Serve as a consultant to donors on the tax advantage of various types of gifts.
Plan and host campus visits for donors or potential donors and their representatives.

Management -

Provide mentorship and professional development opportunities to enhance fundraising effectiveness and career growth.
Set clear performance goals and metrics to ensure alignment with the college’s strategic fundraising priorities.
Conduct regular one-on-one meetings to review progress, provide feedback, and address challenges.
Collaborate with Associate and Assistant Directors on donor strategies, portfolio management, and solicitation plans.
Facilitate communication and collaboration among team members to foster a cohesive and high-performing advancement team.
Evaluate performance and provide constructive feedback during annual reviews, ensuring accountability for achieving individual and team fundraising targets.
Encourage innovative approaches to donor engagement and outreach that align with best practices in higher education fundraising.

Program Management -

Develop and prepare solicitation appeals, proposals, and other materials with a focus on gifts of $100,000 or more that, through the clear identification of funding priorities and articulation of the case for support of the college, engender a level of understanding that is conducive to giving and that help achieve the unit’s fundraising goals.
Assist with the coordination of and participation in college alumni and donor engagement, prospecting, recognition, and stewardship events.
Utilize the Advance alumni and donor database to coordinate with other development colleagues, record contact activities, update donor information, record strategic moves management steps, and gift documentation.
Build working relationships with internal constituents to enhance information exchange between units within the college, including advising faculty and administrators on appropriate fundraising strategies.
Serve as a primary development liaison with several units within the college and will identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward alumni and friends of CANR, MSUE, and AgBioResearch, as well as business, industry, and foundations, in support of the Land Grant mission and the units' priorities.

Communication and Stewardship -

Cultivate, engage, and train Michigan State University alumni, leadership, and employees as potential donors and volunteers.
Engage faculty, department chairs, program directors, and other college leaders in order to assist in the understanding and implementation of fundraising procedures, to seek their advice on funding needs, to answer development questions, to advise them on development strategy, and to solicit them as potential donors; and
Obtain advice and counsel from peers across the enterprise in order to coordinate the cultivation and solicitation of donor prospects.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED
: Direction is received from the Senior Director of Development for the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.

Minimum Requirements

Knowledge equivalent to that which normally would be acquired by completing a four-year college degree program in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing and/or Business; three to five years of related and progressively more responsible or expansive work experience in public relations, volunteer administration, professional and higher education fund raising, marketing or related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Desired Qualifications

Experience managing front-line fundraisers.
Candidates should have a proven track record of driving six-figure gifts to business deals with demonstrative experiences closing gifts.
Experience working with leadership to develop fundraising priorities.
Experience working on multifaceted gift conversations.
Travel involving automobile, airline, and rail.
Possession of a valid vehicle operator’s license at the time of hire.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship, age, disability or protected veteran status.

Required Application Materials

Resume and cover letter

Special Instructions

Interested in joining the team at Michigan State University? For questions, contact Patricia Karam, Director of Talent Acquisition, at karampat@msu.edu.

Work Hours

8 am - 5 pm with possible evenings and weekends

Website

Advancement.msu.edu

MSU strives to provide a flexible work environment, and this position has been designated as remote-friendly. Remote-friendly means some or all of the duties can be performed remotely as mutually agreed upon.

jobs.description:
Managing Director, BerkeleyHaas Ventures

UC Berkeley, Haas School of Business

About the Fund

The Haas School of Business is seeking a venture capitalist to lead BerkeleyHaas Ventures, conceived as a seed/early-stage venture capital fund affiliated with but not owned by the UC Berkeley Haas School of Business. The fund is an institutional venture capital fund measured on financial return. It is the latest in a series of "shared carry" funds, splitting its carried interest with the school. It has among its assets a large alumni pool of potential investors, the most prolific platform for founders and company startups, and a network of students to support the efforts of the fund.

The Fund has four core mandates:
Earn top quartile economic returns and contribute to economic upside for BerkeleyHaas through shared carry
Build an enduring platform and reputable, desired fund brand
Identify, fund, and support enterprises with a connection to UC Berkeley
Deepen student engagement alongside faculty via hands-on, meaningful venture capital process participation

Position Overview

The Managing Director is the lead investment professional and operational leader of the fund, responsible for all aspects and assets of the fund. Among the assets are the BerkeleyHaas brand, pre-primed LP investors, a world-class network of entrepreneurs, investors, and alumni, and a faculty-supported set of students learning and delivering associate level output. An Advisory Committee composed of BerkeleyHaas Board members and faculty with deep investing experience will assist in managing the Berkeley Haas relationship, class instruction and introductions to the fund. This is a high-impact and high-visibility role that blends professional venture investing with a commitment to education, mentorship, and institutional partnership. The GP will leverage Berkeley’s assets to build and sustain the fund: raising capital, sourcing and executing investments with student participation, and enriching UC Berkeley relationships.

The Managing Director and the fund will exemplify BerkeleyHaas’ four Defining Leadership Principles: (1) Question the status quo; (2) Confidence without attitude; (3) Students always; and (4) Beyond yourself.

Advantages

With a close link to BerkeleyHaas, the fund will have advantages to help it outperform. UC Berkeley once again graduated more entrepreneurs than any school in the world. Existing students can become part of associated class curriculum that teaches them how to create value in the venture ecosystem. Work space is possible at the eHub. An alumni network with verified interest in investing in the fund.

Key Responsibilities

Fund Operations & Investment Management

Own the full investment lifecycle: thesis development, sourcing, diligence, negotiations, investment committee, portfolio monitoring, and exit management
Manage fund administration, LP relations, reporting, and compliance in coordination with fund counsel and administrators

Fundraising

Complete capital-raising activities: Follow up on current discussions, new LP identification, outreach, pitching, and close
Develop and maintain fund materials (pitch decks, PPMs, due diligence packages, track record documentation) and ongoing LP communications
Leverage the Berkeley network and personal network of relationships to attract institutional LPs, family offices, and individual investors

Student Engagement & Education

With BerkeleyHaas faculty, support a structured student associate program providing hands-on exposure to sourcing, diligence, and investment committee participation. The degree of support versus lead will vary depending on the candidate
Support BerkeleyHaas faculty in courses covering venture capital, entrepreneurial finance, and new venture strategy
Mentor students interested in VC careers and represent the fund at BerkeleyHaas recruiting events and conferences

Berkeley Entrepreneurship Support

Proactively source investment opportunities with a Berkeley connection
Provide post-investment support to founders: introductions to follow-on investors, customers, and talent; board or advisory participation; and ongoing strategic counsel
Serve as an ambassador for Berkeley entrepreneurship

Required Qualifications

Minimum 5 years of experience in venture capital or equivalent
Deep familiarity with the venture fund lifecycle or demonstrated skills in fundraising, opportunity recognition, and company support and guidance
Demonstrated desire to support educational engagement: mentoring, teaching, or developing early-career talent in investment or entrepreneurship contexts
Existing relationships within the venture ecosystem: investors, founders, advisors, accelerators, legal and finance advisory
Ability to operate as a Managing Director: self-directed, highly organized, and comfortable managing multiple workstreams with limited administrative support
Excellent judgment, integrity, and alignment with the academic values and reputational standards of UC Berkeley and Haas
Strong verbal communication skills: investment recommendations, LP stakeholder communications.

Differentiating Qualifications

MBA or advanced degree preferred (UC Berkeley affiliation a plus)
Additional communications skills: navigating the decision process of a CVC, academic instruction
Operating experience as a founder or early-stage executive, providing credibility and empathy when working with student entrepreneurs
Active network within the UC Berkeley community (alumni, faculty relationships, or prior campus engagement)

What Success Looks Like

In Year 1 to 3, success means: fund one closed and deployed into a high-quality early portfolio; a functioning and highly sought student program with faculty; and strong relationships established with LPs, BerkeleyHaas faculty and campus entrepreneurship infrastructure.
Over the fund lifecycle, success means: a portfolio of Berkeley-connected companies that go on to raise follow-on capital and create real outcomes; students who credit the program as formative to their VC careers; and a track record that supports raising a successor fund, delivering carried interest to both the GP and BerkeleyHaas.
The ultimate success is a series of larger and increasingly successful funds creating value for the Managing Director, BerkeleyHaas, and students.

Compensation & Economics

The Managing Partner will receive market-rate management fees commensurate with fund size, and will split carried interest with BerkeleyHaas in recognition of the institutional affiliation, brand value, and programmatic resources provided.

This structure is designed to create genuine financial alignment: the GP is motivated to maximize fund returns, and BerkeleyHaas shares in that upside as a long-term institutional partner.

In this results-oriented position, you’ll play a critical role in shaping the future of STEM education and research. You’ll leverage your strategic thinking and interpersonal skills to cultivate relationships with alumni and friends, securing vital resources that fuel innovation and opportunity in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.

What will you do?

Become a champion for the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources and Michigan State University by raising support for cutting-edge research with a real-world impact across multiple fields: You’ll manage a portfolio of 75 - 100 prospects, fostering long-term relationships that elevate the College’s reputation and fuel its success.
Uncover hidden potential: Employ your keen eye for discovery to identify new alumni and donors, building a robust pipeline for future giving.
Leverage your strategic planning experience: Develop and execute personalized cultivation and stewardship strategies, averaging 12-15 strategic face-to-face visits and 2-4 solicitations per month.

Be a part of and learn from a team dedicated to building a cohesive culture: Work alongside a high-performing development team, sharing best practices and celebrating collective achievements.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

Join a collaborative environment: We foster a supportive and team-oriented atmosphere where you’ll be empowered to grow and excel.
Be part of a prestigious institution: You’ll have the privilege of donning Spartan green and white, while representing the land grant mission to provide high-quality education, conduct research, and engage with the public to advance knowledge and improve lives.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Director of Development will manage a portfolio of 75-100 major and principal gift donor prospects, focusing efforts on prospects whose philanthropic capacity is $100,000 or more to maximize the fundraising potential within the College and on behalf of Michigan State University. Additionally, the Director will oversee and manage the Associate and Assistant Directors of Development, providing leadership, mentorship, and strategic direction to ensure their success in advancing the college's development goals.

The Director will average 12-15 strategic visits per month, resulting in greater engagement and movement toward a major gift solicitation at a rate of 2 to 4 solicitations per month, with all solicitation efforts cleared and coordinated with the college and University Advancement at Michigan State University. A significant amount of the Director’s time will be dedicated to traveling out of state and managing prospect activity within a few major metro areas.

The duties of the Director of Development are as follows, but are not limited to:

Fundraising -

Engage in the identification, cultivation, and solicitation of gifts, mainly from individuals, as well as some corporations and professional groups in support of the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources' strategic and campaign priorities.
Collaborate and coordinate with University Advancement, administrators, and faculty in the college to create and carry out fundraising strategies and solicitation of gifts of $100,000 and more.
Identify and maintain an active pool of 75 prospects under strategic management.
Achieve college fundraising goals through an active and consistent program of prospect and donor outreach that includes 180 significant contacts annually.
Utilize phone calls, email, mail, social media, and other strategies to identify, connect with, and engage alumni with the goal of soliciting financial support.
Identify, qualify, and work to build strong, engaged relationships with major gift prospects to determine and merge prospect passions, interests, and needs with the college’s funding priority areas.

Evaluate performance and provide constructive feedback during annual reviews, ensuring accountability for achieving individual and team fundraising targets.
Encourage innovative approaches to donor engagement and outreach that align with best practices in higher education fundraising.

Program Management -

Develop and prepare solicitation appeals, proposals, and other materials with a focus on gifts of $100,000 or more that, through the clear identification of funding priorities and articulation of the case for support of the college, engender a level of understanding that is conducive to giving and that help achieve the unit’s fundraising goals.

Managing Director, BerkeleyHaas Ventures

UC Berkeley, Haas School of Business

About the Fund

The Haas School of Business is seeking a venture capitalist to lead BerkeleyHaas Ventures, conceived as a seed/early-stage venture capital fund affiliated with but not owned by the UC Berkeley Haas School of Business. The fund is an institutional venture capital fund measured on financial return. It is the latest in a series of "shared carry" funds, splitting its carried interest with the school. It has among its assets a large alumni pool of potential investors, the most prolific platform for founders and company startups, and a network of students to support the efforts of the fund.

The Fund has four core mandates:
Earn top quartile economic returns and contribute to economic upside for BerkeleyHaas through shared carry
Build an enduring platform and reputable, desired fund brand
Identify, fund, and support enterprises with a connection to UC Berkeley
Deepen student engagement alongside faculty via hands-on, meaningful venture capital process participation

Position Overview

The Managing Director is the lead investment professional and operational leader of the fund, responsible for all aspects and assets of the fund. Among the assets are the BerkeleyHaas brand, pre-primed LP investors, a world-class network of entrepreneurs, investors, and alumni, and a faculty-supported set of students learning and delivering associate level output. An Advisory Committee composed of BerkeleyHaas Board members and faculty with deep investing experience will assist in managing the Berkeley Haas relationship, class instruction and introductions to the fund. This is a high-impact and high-visibility role that blends professional venture investing with a commitment to education, mentorship, and institutional partnership. The GP will leverage Berkeley’s assets to build and sustain the fund: raising capital, sourcing and executing investments with student participation, and enriching UC Berkeley relationships.

The Managing Director and the fund will exemplify BerkeleyHaas’ four Defining Leadership Principles: (1) Question the status quo; (2) Confidence without attitude; (3) Students always; and (4) Beyond yourself.

Advantages

With a close link to BerkeleyHaas, the fund will have advantages to help it outperform. UC Berkeley once again graduated more entrepreneurs than any school in the world. Existing students can become part of associated class curriculum that teaches them how to create value in the venture ecosystem. Work space is possible at the eHub. An alumni network with verified interest in investing in the fund.

Key Responsibilities

Fund Operations & Investment Management

Own the full investment lifecycle: thesis development, sourcing, diligence, negotiations, investment committee, portfolio monitoring, and exit management
Manage fund administration, LP relations, reporting, and compliance in coordination with fund counsel and administrators

Fundraising

Complete capital-raising activities: Follow up on current discussions, new LP identification, outreach, pitching, and close
Develop and maintain fund materials (pitch decks, PPMs, due diligence packages, track record documentation) and ongoing LP communications
Leverage the Berkeley network and personal network of relationships to attract institutional LPs, family offices, and individual investors

Student Engagement & Education

With BerkeleyHaas faculty, support a structured student associate program providing hands-on exposure to sourcing, diligence, and investment committee participation. The degree of support versus lead will vary depending on the candidate
Support BerkeleyHaas faculty in courses covering venture capital, entrepreneurial finance, and new venture strategy
Mentor students interested in VC careers and represent the fund at BerkeleyHaas recruiting events and conferences

Berkeley Entrepreneurship Support

Proactively source investment opportunities with a Berkeley connection
Provide post-investment support to founders: introductions to follow-on investors, customers, and talent; board or advisory participation; and ongoing strategic counsel
Serve as an ambassador for Berkeley entrepreneurship

Required Qualifications

Minimum 5 years of experience in venture capital or equivalent
Deep familiarity with the venture fund lifecycle or demonstrated skills in fundraising, opportunity recognition, and company support and guidance
Demonstrated desire to support educational engagement: mentoring, teaching, or developing early-career talent in investment or entrepreneurship contexts
Existing relationships within the venture ecosystem: investors, founders, advisors, accelerators, legal and finance advisory
Ability to operate as a Managing Director: self-directed, highly organized, and comfortable managing multiple workstreams with limited administrative support
Excellent judgment, integrity, and alignment with the academic values and reputational standards of UC Berkeley and Haas
Strong verbal communication skills: investment recommendations, LP stakeholder communications.

Differentiating Qualifications

MBA or advanced degree preferred (UC Berkeley affiliation a plus)
Additional communications skills: navigating the decision process of a CVC, academic instruction
Operating experience as a founder or early-stage executive, providing credibility and empathy when working with student entrepreneurs
Active network within the UC Berkeley community (alumni, faculty relationships, or prior campus engagement)

What Success Looks Like

In Year 1 to 3, success means: fund one closed and deployed into a high-quality early portfolio; a functioning and highly sought student program with faculty; and strong relationships established with LPs, BerkeleyHaas faculty and campus entrepreneurship infrastructure.
Over the fund lifecycle, success means: a portfolio of Berkeley-connected companies that go on to raise follow-on capital and create real outcomes; students who credit the program as formative to their VC careers; and a track record that supports raising a successor fund, delivering carried interest to both the GP and BerkeleyHaas.
The ultimate success is a series of larger and increasingly successful funds creating value for the Managing Director, BerkeleyHaas, and students.

Compensation & Economics

The Managing Partner will receive market-rate management fees commensurate with fund size, and will split carried interest with BerkeleyHaas in recognition of the institutional affiliation, brand value, and programmatic resources provided.

This structure is designed to create genuine financial alignment: the GP is motivated to maximize fund returns, and BerkeleyHaas shares in that upside as a long-term institutional partner.

Chief Operating Officer

Taltran Global has been exclusively engaged by a privately held real estate investment and operating platform led by a highly respected, industry-known owner and investor with a decades-long track record of building one of the most notable legacy property portfolios in the U.S., with significant holdings across the East Coast.

The firm is in an exciting stage of transition and evolution, actively repositioning its portfolio toward higher cash-flow markets in the Southeast while optimizing a long-standing and highly successful real estate platform. With a lean but highly experienced structure and long-tenured external partners, this is a rare opportunity to step directly into a right-hand role to the owner and help shape the next phase of the business.

What sets this opportunity apart is the ability to step into a highly visible, strategic leadership role within a tightly held, entrepreneurial investment platform. You will work directly with the owner and key advisors while helping drive portfolio strategy, leasing execution, cash flow optimization, and investment decision-making across a complex multi-asset real estate portfolio.

Responsibilities:

The Chief Operating Officer will provide broad operational and strategic leadership across the company's real estate holdings and related business activities. This individual will be expected to operate with a high degree of independence and help translate the owner's objectives into actionable strategies and measurable results.

The position is based in Southeast Florida with some periodic travel.

·         Act as the right hand to the Owner/President, supporting all strategic and operational decisions

Oversee day-to-day real estate operations across the full portfolio

Drive portfolio strategy and cash flow optimization (6-8% target yield)

Help lead the company's strategy for 1031 exchanges and geographic repositioning, including the transition of selected Massachusetts assets toward Southeastern Florida

Source, evaluate, structure, and execute acquisitions, dispositions, and investment opportunities

Oversee leasing strategy, negotiations, and renewals across all asset types

Manage asset performance, including budgeting, forecasting, and reporting (actual vs. budget)

Lead or support refinancing, recapitalizations, and lender relationships

Oversee external partners including brokers, attorneys, accountants, and property managers

Improve operational systems, reporting, and internal infrastructure across a lean platform

What We’re Looking For:

8-15+ years of experience in real estate operations, asset management, investments, or development

Strong experience in leasing, lease negotiations, and portfolio management

Exposure to 1031 exchanges, acquisitions/dispositions, and capital structuring

Strong financial acumen across cash flow, ROI, and asset-level decision-making

Experience working directly with owners or senior leadership

Ability to thrive in a lean, entrepreneurial, high-autonomy environment

Why This Role:

This position offers a rare opportunity to work directly with an established real estate owner and investor and to play a meaningful role in the continued evolution of a substantial legacy portfolio.

The COO will have significant visibility with ownership, broad exposure to investment and operating decisions, and the autonomy to improve how the organization functions. The role is particularly well suited to an executive who enjoys working in an entrepreneurial environment, prefers direct access to decision-makers, and wants to have a tangible impact on both portfolio performance and long-term investment strategy.

Position Summary

Responsible for day-to-day operations of the community. Assures compliance with all laws, rules, regulations, policies, and procedures. Oversight of property management, Employee Partner administration, and provision of Resident Services. Promotes the company’s mission and philosophy.

REPORTS TO:
REGIONAL DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS

Position Responsibilities

Resident Services
Assures implementation of policies and procedures relating to Resident care.
Supervises and assists in provision of all Resident services, including the coordination of those provided by independently contracted ancillary health care providers as requested by Residents and families.
Conducts assessments, negotiates service plans, develops service schedules, and updates service information as indicates by Resident need.
Ensures that Residents are appropriately assessed on a timely basis and charged in accordance with that assessment.
Assists Residents to participate in self-governance activity through Resident council and committee meetings.
Acts as an advocate for Residents and maintains communication with designated agents as requested and required.
Assures quality of Resident services.
Assures a high degree of customer satisfaction at residence. Promptly investigates complaints and reports findings and appropriate recommendation to the President of SSL Management Company. Ensures follow-up communication occurs to complainant and that substantiated complaints are resolved to reasonable satisfaction of complainant.
Ensures compliance with all rules and regulations related to Resident care (i.e., HIPAA, State Regulations and OSHA, etc.).
Maintains a professional demeanor with all Residents and their loved ones.

Employee Partner Administration
Recruits, interviews, hires, supervises, evaluates, and disciplines community Employee Partners.
Assures the availability of qualified, appropriately trained community Employee Partners.
Supervises and assists in orientation and training of community Employee Partners.
Coordinates and assists in administration of wages/benefits for community Employee Partners, assures accuracy of Employee Partner records and approves payment for work performed.
Assures Employee Partners’ adherence to all policies and procedures, all work, safety, and administrative rules.
Ensures compliance with all rules and regulations related to Employee Partners (i.e., OSHA, Wage & Hours, FMLA, etc.).
Promotes the company’s mission and philosophy.
Maintains a professional demeanor with all Employee Partners.

Sales/Marketing
Develops and implements sales/marketing plans with President of SSL Management Company and Sales Team to accomplish occupancy targets.
Develops and maintains a favorable public image; participates in community organizations for the promotion of the community and SSL.
Provides external marketing efforts on a weekly basis.
Meets sales/marketing goals or adjusts sales plans accordingly to accomplish occupancy targets.

Property Management
Coordinates community, Resident units, common areas, and adjacent grounds with Maintenance Director.

Financial Responsibility
Operates with resources provided, assures income and expenses are controlled using annual budget projections.
Assures all financial records are properly maintained.
Participates in the development of an annual budget.
Assures that Resident invoices are delivered, and the residence’s accounts receivables are collected on a timely, consistent basis.

Administrative Responsibility
Administrates, coordinates, and directs all activities in accordance with policies and procedures.
Assures safety and security of community’s contents and inhabitants (Residents, Employee Partners, and visitors).
Assures proper use of equipment/supplies.
Maintains and provides all data as requested, required.
Will be on call; arranges appropriate coverage when absent from community or unavailable to respond to emergencies.
Performs other duties as assigned or required.
Assures that adverse findings by company Quality reviews or state surveyors are promptly corrected and remain in compliance.

Employment Requirements

Effective supervisory skills.
Ability to communicate and work with all levels of the company’s Employee Partners effectively.
Ability to recognize and communicate problems appropriately.
Ability to relate to the public, Residents, families, Employee Partners, and other professionals appropriately.
Ability to maintain accurate records and provide information as requested and required.
Ability to communicate proficiently in English, verbally and in writing.
Ability to work flexible hours to meet requirements of the job and be on call.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, 30 pounds regularly.
Maintains car in good working order, current driver’s license in good standing and auto insurance meeting company minimums is current.
CPR certified.
Ability to teach/train others effectively.

Training And Experience

Experience in managing a program or community for older adults preferred. One year of supervisory experience required. Knowledge of an interest in working with older adults required. Holds a current CPR Certificate or can obtain a CPR Certificate within 90 days of being hired.

Education

High school diploma required. College credits or degree preferred or sufficient education to satisfy state experience requirement. Maintain CPR/First Aid Certification. Attendance at mandatory in-service training. Meet continuing education requirements on job classification and position.
